title: Campaign music: feel sketches for five films

steps.path: What we took from your last music review
steps.headline: Your real complaint was never "busy": it was parts that did not sound like one piece of music.
steps.changed: In your words: "different instruments playing entirely their own song at different volume levels", a tune "randomly thrown in on top", high notes "thrown-in", strings "wayyy too harsh". A full sound is fine when it is one song. Settled from your picks: our soft piano, middle brightness, today's room, rich chords, both pulses you liked, quiet or piano-only endings, no strings.
steps.notice: The long music guide is now a two-page brief that starts with "one piece of music, not layers": every part follows the same chords, the tune is the top line of the same piano, parts stay close in volume and rise and fall together. Process, as you approved: two 15-second sketches per film, you pick, then the full score. Five different films are tested, not one.

steps.headline: Which feel should Make it mine's full score use: straight or gently swung?
steps.today: Two 15-second sketches over the same stretch of the re-cut film. Same notes, same tempo (128 beats a minute, a step faster than before because you said this film needs more energy). A: the piano pattern moves in even, straight steps, which drives forward. B: every second note comes a little late, so it bounces instead of drives.
steps.problem: Listen for whether the piano pattern, the soft pad and the tune sound like one piece played by one pair of hands, and which feel suits how quickly this film moves. Honest doubt: nobody here can hear; this was judged from note lists and measurements only. The tune's notes all fit the chords, but the pad's volume does not yet rise and fall with the piano's, so the pad may still feel like a separate layer. It is also a little brighter than your "middle" pick.

steps.headline: Which feel should the purple film use: steady at 120, or quicker and bouncier at 132?
steps.today: A: steady and straight at 120 beats a minute, the piano's even pulse with the tune running along the top in one unbroken line as the colours speed up, ending on the name played by the same soft piano. B: the same notes a step faster (132) with a gentle bounce; the card's fastest colour changes bounce with it.
steps.problem: Listen for whether the music speeds up with the colours as one piece of piano music, and whether the name feels like the tune's own last note. The loudness stays fairly even, so the build may feel steady rather than exciting, and the tune is there a bit more of the time than in your favourite pieces. The card's font is a stand-in.

steps.headline: Under the narrator's close, which blends better: a soft held sound under the piano, or the piano alone?
steps.today: This pair asks about texture, not tempo: both are 115.65 beats a minute, straight (the tempo nearest your "120 with breaths" that puts both scene cuts on bar lines). A: a soft held sound carries the chords under a light, high piano tick. B: the same notes, all on one piano, its chord played again every bar instead of the held sound.
steps.problem: Listen for whether A's held sound blends in as part of one piece, or B, all one piano, sounds more like a single piece. Both grow toward the wall of screens, go quiet under her last words and end on the same quiet piano name. Honest doubt: judged from note lists only. Two of her short words sit only about 3 dB over the music, and the swell is small (about 1.3 dB) and may be too subtle to notice.

steps.intro: From "However, recently..." to "...artificial intelligence.", where the page glows on "wonderful". These two sketches are also the evidence for the narrator question on the next page.

steps.headline: Should the music meet her quick, bright read, or give her room and soften her slightly?
steps.today: A, meet her energy: a little quicker (124 beats a minute), gently swung, all one piano, soft chords on every bar and their own notes repeated higher; her voice exactly as recorded. B, give her room: your steady 120, a quiet held pad and a low bass note while she talks, two soft piano notes only in her longer pauses, her pauses a little longer, and her voice made slightly softer and set a touch further back.
steps.problem: Listen for where her read feels at home, and whether each sounds like one piece. Honest doubt: judged from note lists only. Her speed and pitch are unchanged in both, so if both still feel wrong, the read itself is the likelier cause. In both her pauses are up to 0.67 s longer, with the picture holding still to match. A's high notes still sit about an octave over the chords while she speaks, and both are a little brighter than your "middle" pick.
steps.proposal: Pick the approach to score in full. Neither means the recording is the problem; the next page asks what to do about it.
